storage.transaction_rule: policy writes are short caller transactions; never hold a transaction while invoking a backend or waiting on tools

automatic_requires: current time within the explicit focus window
dispatch.private_child: inherits a sealed demand origin decoded from the persisted root frame record; public_demand descendants follow explicit public demand and remain eligible during quiet, while automatic descendants require the current matching focus window and dispatch permission and are suppressed by quiet
dispatch.origin_binding: PowerPolicy.root_demand_origin(root_id) reads pa1_frames.origin_class and returns a typed origin bound to that root; model supplied origin strings are rejected
dispatch.quiet_policy: blocks automatic roots and descendants; an explicit public foreground demand remains eligible
dispatch.release_policy: blocks all dispatch until explicit resume or the operator-declared end, including status checks, restart and new demand; repeated trusted release requests during the same active veto reuse its request ID and preserve verified physical proof while optional metadata changes are applied
dispatch.priority: foreground versus opportunistic is returned as scheduling metadata; the scheduler owns ordering and slot limits

operator_control.authority: typed process-local TrustedOperatorControl and OperatorPermission objects; role strings, model output and source text cannot grant authority
operator_control.status: snapshot is read-only and never calls the backend

release_contract.intent: set_release persists the logical rewarming veto and physical_state=pending before returning ReleaseIntent
release_contract.delivery: deliver_release_intent requires the caller transaction to be committed; callbacks must be idempotent by request_id and must not be called while a DB transaction is open
release_contract.failure: callback failure leaves the veto and physical_state=pending
release_contract.accounting: no callback result or caller receipt is treated as proof; ResourceController checks the committed complete tracked-session set and exact owner proof, then mints a typed acknowledgement bound to request_id; PowerPolicy records released_verified only from that provider
release_contract.verified_state: physical_state, verification time, nonempty verified session count, owner-proof digest, and target-set digest persist across restart; logical rewarming veto remains until its declared end or explicit resume

expiry_and_focus.quiet: expiry is stored with the quiet window; the first scheduling decision after expiry persists the cleared state, so later focus changes or a backwards wall-clock adjustment cannot revive it
expiry_and_focus.automatic_focus: one explicit focus/project window; duration is at least one second and at most 86400 seconds; non-finite boundaries are rejected; dispatch checks exact focus and project and clears an observed expired window durably
expiry_and_focus.status: expired state is reported effectively without mutation; expiry is persisted by scheduling policy checks

coverage: root origin read from the real FrameStore schema and preserved across restart
quiet expiry and no focus resurrection
public-demand and automatic-origin child inheritance, root binding, and quiet suppression
release veto across process restart and new demand
post-commit release callback contract and pending failure
typed owner proof bridge records released state without clearing logical veto
declared release end and explicit resume preserve physical pending state
NaN and infinite quiet, release, and focus timestamps rejected; focus window minimum and 24-hour maximum enforced
owner verifies all committed session proofs, persists physical release state, and retains logical veto across restart
partial and replaced owner proof cannot mark physical release verified
empty/unbound owner proof cannot mark physical release verified
repeat clicks and metadata updates preserve the active intent and verified proof
resume and expiry end idempotency and require a new physical proof
new owner target invalidates prior physical proof under the active veto
